items.rationale: Lightning overvoltage is covered under 2.3.3. The unit is about 7 m from the hob, so the 5 m exclusion in 2.3.10(c) does not apply. It is a fixed, wired installation that could not be repaired, so a like-for-like replacement is due under 7.1.1(c) and 7.1.9(a).
The unit is climate-control equipment a couple of metres from the hob, inside 5 m. Overvoltage damage to it is excluded outright by 2.3.10(c), and no kitchen climate endorsement is on the schedule.

The wording supports cover: 7.1.9(c) pays the labour of fitting a replacement for an affected installation, and 7.1.11 lets the charge follow its covered principal. Against that, the price history shows this line type unpaid in all 4 earlier cases, possibly because the floor unit was treated as not firmly connected, so cover is uncertain.
This is an ancillary charge to the excluded kitchen unit, so it falls with its principal item under 7.1.11 and 3.5(e).
The existing stand was scorched and cannot be reused. An equivalent support needed to set the replacement in place is covered under 7.1.9(b).
Ordinary carriage is covered under 7.1.9(e) and 7.1.12, but it relates to both units. Under 7.1.11 it is apportioned by value, so roughly half (the living-room unit's share) is indemnified.
